description: Helps you decide which customer segment to back, and whether your pricing is safe if AI cuts seats: it takes each segment's ACV, sales cycle, accounts, deal source and CAC, its logo, gross and net retention, how you charge in your own words, and your seller ramp, cost and qualified demand, and returns one page per segment with payback, gross profit per dollar of CAC, seller capacity after ramp and cycle, and the renewal if customers cut a share of seats. Ask the person to confirm the segment split, their own win rate and what customers can cut before marking each as confirmed; anything not confirmed or not given is shown as missing, never guessed.

business_stage.description: Optional: funding stage, passed to the motion first draft (for example series-a)

confirmed.description: What the person has confirmed. Set each to true only after asking them. Until the segment split is confirmed no sum runs

seat_cut.description: The person confirmed what customers can cut, and the share of seats to test

segment_split.description: The person confirmed the segments are how their closed deals really divide

win_rate.description: The person confirmed the win rates are their own, from closed deals

gross_margin_percent.description: Gross margin as a percent (for example 72). Needed for payback and every profit sum

industry.description: Optional: your industry, passed to the motion first draft

product.description: What you sell, in one line

segments.description: One item per customer segment (1 to 4). Split by who signs, how they find you, sales cycle and contract value

accounts.description: Number of accounts that could buy in this segment

acv.description: Average contract value per year, in dollars

arr_share_cutting_percent.description: Optional: the percent of this segment's revenue held by accounts that would make that cut (for example 32)

buyer_cost_per_seat_per_year.description: Optional: what one seat costs the buyer in a year, in salary and overhead, in dollars

cac.description: Cost to win one customer in this segment, in dollars

churn_reasons.description: Optional: why customers in this segment leave or shrink, in their words, separated by semicolons

deal_source.description: Where most deals in this segment come from (for example inbound, outbound, referrals, partnerships or mixed)

gross_retention_gate_percent.description: Optional: your own gross retention line for releasing more money (for example 90)

gross_retention_percent.description: Gross revenue retention as a percent: opening revenue less churn and downgrades, over opening revenue (for example 92). It cannot pass 100

icp_match_percent.description: Optional: percent of accounts that match your ideal customer profile, passed to the sizing first draft

logo_retention_gate_percent.description: Optional: your own logo retention line (for example 85)

logo_retention_percent.description: Share of customers still paying after a year, as a percent (for example 89)

monthly_logo_churn_percent.description: Optional: share of customers lost in a month, as a percent (for example 2.5). Used for the simple lifetime sum; left out, yearly logo retention is used

monthly_qualified_demand.description: Qualified opportunities assigned to sellers each month in this segment

motion_lead.description: Optional: the lead motion from the EPIC audit on GTM Alpha, as it came back

motion_reason.description: Optional: the audit's reason line for the lead motion, as it came back

motion_score.description: Optional: the score of that lead motion, 1 to 10

name.description: The segment in your own words (for example 'banks and insurers with 200 to 2,000 contact centre agents')

net_retention_gate_percent.description: Optional: your own net retention line (for example 100)

net_retention_percent.description: Net revenue retention as a percent: gross retention plus expansion (for example 108)

pricing_unit.description: Optional: the pricing unit, if you want to state it directly. It overrides the reading of your sentence

pricing_unit_in_writing.description: What you bill on, in your own words (for example 'per agent seat, billed yearly' or 'per resolved contact')

ramped_deals_per_seller_per_year.description: Deals a fully ramped seller closes in a year in this segment, from your own record

run_cost_per_unit.description: Optional: your cost to run one unit of work, in dollars

sales_cycle_days.description: Days from first meeting to signature

seat_cut_percent.description: Optional: the percent of seats a customer could cut if AI does more of the work (for example 25). Used only when the person has confirmed it

seat_share_of_acv_percent.description: Optional, for a mix of seats and usage: the percent of the contract billed on seats (for example 60)

seats_per_account.description: Optional: seats in an average account

seller_loaded_cost_per_year.description: Full yearly cost of one seller, in dollars

seller_ramp_months.description: Months before a new seller carries a full pipeline

sizing_sam.description: Optional: SAM in dollars from the sizing calculator

sizing_som.description: Optional: year one SOM in dollars from the sizing calculator

sizing_tam.description: Optional: TAM in dollars from the sizing calculator on ICP Intelligence

sizing_year_one_customers.description: Optional: customers needed in year one, from the sizing calculator

usage_price_per_unit.description: Optional: a price per unit of work you want to test, in dollars

what_customers_can_cut.description: What a customer can cut, and when, in your own words (for example 'seats, at each yearly renewal')

win_rate_percent.description: Your own win rate: the percent of qualified opportunities you win in this segment, from your closed deals (for example 33). Used only when the person has confirmed it

work_units_per_seat_per_year.description: Optional: units of work one seat handles in a year (for example contacts, shipments or claims)

year_one_customer_target.description: Optional: new customers you want from this segment in year one. Left out, the customer count from the sizing first draft is used

year_one_share_percent.description: Optional: the year one share you assume, as a percent, passed to the sizing first draft

tracks_expansion.description: Optional: true only if the company tracks expansion account by account. It adds a later years table below the pages. Payback on CAC and ARR always leads

name: segment_and_seat_cut_check
title: Segment and Seat Cut Check
